newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA TIGHTEN GRIP BUT LOSE ELLIOTT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA TIGHTEN GRIP BUT LOSE ELLIOTT.

text.p: Australia tightened their grip on the second test against West Indies on Monday after opener Matthew Elliott was denied a likely maiden test century because of injury.
Elliott was forced to retire hurt because of a knee injury with his score on 78 after a painful collision with batting partner Mark Waugh at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
Waugh made amends for his involvement in the incident by scoring a disciplined 67 as Australia crawled to 224 for three at tea on the fourth day, a lead of 251 runs.
With four sessions left to play, Australia captain Mark Taylor is left with a tricky decision over the timing of his declaration. He is expected to set West Indies a target of about 300 runs.
Australia struggled to score quickly on a slow wicket against accurate bowling. Only 147 runs were added during the first two sessions after they started the day on 77 for two.
Elliott and Waugh collided as they sprinted between the wickets in search of a second run with the total on 143 for two just before lunch.

Although both batsmen were knocked to the ground, Elliott managed to dive back to the safety of his crease, foiling West Indies' attempt to run him out. But he was unable to carry on batting after lengthy treatment.
Waugh was caught behind by wicketkeeper Courtney Browne before tea to give fast bowler Curtly Ambrose his first wicket of the match.
Elliot will undergo further tests on his right knee but he is highly unlikely to bat again in the match, an Australian Cricket Board spokesman told reporters.
It was cruel luck for Elliott, who was selected for the first test in Brisbane as a replacement for out-of-form opener Michael Slater.
Australia, who won the first test by 123 runs, scored 331 in their first innings in Sydney before dismissing West Indies for 304.
